newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Slightly weaker in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Slightly weaker in thin talk.

text.p: Recovery in crude values failed to help sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Wednesday, traders said.
A lack of fresh buying interest would keep market activity slow in the near term.
A major was heard offering the 180-cst grade for late June/early July lifting at $101.00 per tonne but the bid was seen at $100.50, traders said.
"Prices will just move around current levels without much change, unless someting unexpected comes up" said one trader.
Some Korean refineries are still being shut down for maintenance in June and Kuwait has slowed down its exports due to domestic summer demand, tightening the supply side, traders said.
"Supplies are tighter but at the same time demand is pretty poor, so the market is balanced at the moment," said one trader.
Petron Corp, Philippines' biggest oil refiner, has issued a tender to buy 200,000 barrels (27,000 tonnes) of 180-cst fuel oil for July delivery, a company source said.
The tender, which seeks fuel oil with sulphur content of 1.0-1.7 percent for delivery July 6-10, will close on July 13 and is valid on the same day.
In the swaps market on late Wednesday, July swaps were at $99.00/$99.55 against Tuesday's $99.25/$99.75. August swaps were at $99.00/$99.75 against $98.25/$99.00.
The SIMEX fuel oil futures contract remained untraded for the second day, with July bid/offered at $98.30/$100.00.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
